standard.title: Draw conclusions and make proposals
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1S05): Students drew evidence-based conclusions about change and made proposals for caring for places.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students draw conclusions about local significance, technology change and place connections, and make proposals for positive futures.

nodes.label: Drawing conclusions about significance and change
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can draw conclusions about local significance, how technology impacted people's lives, and how people are connected to local and distant places.
nodes.minimum_width: Draw at least one conclusion about either local significance, technology change or place connections, supported by evidence.
nodes.typical_width: List what makes a local person, place or building significant and conclude how people are connected to it; use Venn diagrams or tables to show continuity/change in technology over time; discuss how a technology change impacted work, travel or communication.
wider: Draw conclusions from a Venn diagram comparing two technologies across time and explain the pattern of change
Conclude how knowledge of special places and natural systems contributes to caring behaviour and conservation
nodes.hinge_reason: Conclusions are the prerequisite for proposals — students cannot propose meaningful futures without first concluding what matters and why.

response_modes.reason: Making the conclusion explicit (as a statement, not just implied) is the skill being developed — use sentence frames to make conclusions visible before asking for proposals.

success_criteria: States at least one conclusion supported by evidence
Conclusion addresses significance, change or connections as targeted by the inquiry

nodes.label: Proposing positive futures
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can use knowledge of a familiar place or site to imagine how it might change in the future and propose how they could influence a positive future for it.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify one way a familiar place might change and propose one action that could lead to a positive future for it.
nodes.typical_width: Use knowledge about a familiar place or site to imagine two possible futures; propose actions that could lead to positive outcomes; consider who needs to be involved and what resources would be needed.
wider: Develop a proposal for a local place that considers perspectives of at least two different community groups
Forecast a probable future and a preferred future for a local place and explain the difference

response_modes.reason: Future proposals integrate place knowledge, significance understanding, perspective awareness and evidence-based conclusions — it is the Year 2 evaluating endpoint.

success_criteria: Describes at least one possible future for a familiar place
Proposes at least one action to achieve a positive future
